answer_text:
Let

\[
\alpha=1+\sqrt2,\qquad \beta=1-\sqrt2.
\]

The numbers \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are conjugates, so

\[
\alpha^{3000}+\beta^{3000}
\]

is an integer. Since \(3000\) is even,

\[
\beta^{3000}=(1-\sqrt2)^{3000}=(\sqrt2-1)^{3000}>0.
\]

Let

\[
\varepsilon=(\sqrt2-1)^{3000}.
\]

Then

\[
(1+\sqrt2)^{3000}=\alpha^{3000}
= \bigl(\alpha^{3000}+\beta^{3000}\bigr)-\varepsilon
= M-\varepsilon
\]

for some integer \(M\). Since \(0<\varepsilon<1\), the fractional part of \((1+\sqrt2)^{3000}\) is

\[
1-\varepsilon.
\]

Now estimate \(\varepsilon\). Since \(\sqrt2-1<\frac12\),

\[
\varepsilon=(\sqrt2-1)^{3000}<2^{-3000}.
\]

Also,

\[
2^{10}=1024>10^3,
\]

so

\[
2^{3000}=(2^{10})^{300}>10^{900}>10^{100}.
\]

Thus

\[
\varepsilon<10^{-100}.
\]

Therefore

\[
0<10^{100}\varepsilon<1,
\]

so

\[
10^{100}-1<10^{100}(1-\varepsilon)<10^{100}.
\]

Hence

\[
\left\lfloor 10^{100}(1-\varepsilon)\right\rfloor=10^{100}-1.
\]

The units digit of \(10^{100}-1\) is \(9\), and that is exactly the 100th digit to the right of the decimal point.

\[
\boxed{9}
\]
